newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ wool prices mostly easier at Christchurch sale.
newsitem.headline: NZ wool prices mostly easier at Christchurch sale.

text.p: With the exception of fine wool and some lambs wool, wool prices eased at the sale in Christchurch on Thursday, Wools of New Zealand said.
The market indicator fell six cents to 439 cents with the strong segment also down six to 390, while lamb rose two to 403.
Main buying interest came from China, Nepal and Western Europe, with support from Turkey, Australia and India.

The major changes in prices compared to the last sale were: Merino fleece up to 2.0 percent dearer, crossbred fleece 35 micron and stronger up to 1.5 percent cheaper, cotts average and average/poor styles 4.0-5.0 percent cheaper, second shear par to
2.5 percent cheaper, second lambs 29/30 micron good/average style 2.0 percent dearer and the remainder 2.5 percent cheaper, and bulky skirtings up to 1.5 percent cheaper.

On offer was 1,664 clean tonnes, 65 percent of which was crossbred fleece with 14 percent lambswool, six percent cotts and five percent second shear. The next sales are at Napier and Christchurch on Feb 20. --Wellington Newsroom (64 4) 4734746
